articles.title: Ebenezer review – Johnny Depp’s Scrooge tries to exorcise ghosts of business past
articles.summary: The latest film version of the Dickens classic A Christmas Carol is decent enough, though its star is rather better as the legendary miser before redemption arrives. Here for lovers of Dickens – and fans of subtext – is an unexpectedly watchable new movie version of A Christmas Carol starring a…
body: In fact, screenwriter Nathaniel Halpern and director Ti West have put together a perfectly serviceable, faithful adaptation – a tradaptation, if you will – of Dickens’s masterpiece about the hideous old miser saved from damnation on Christmas Eve by the appearance of three Christmas ghosts, from yuletides past, present and future. It sticks to the accepted narrative beats and more or less all the familiar episodes, but with a few twists.

There is a witty and ingenious new prologue sequence in which Scrooge’s equally grumpy partner Jacob Marley, played by Ian McKellen, is still alive, going into a full Stadler-and-Waldorf double-act with his old colleague. (Wait – did The Muppet Christmas Carol inspire this?) And West shows us his scary-movie style by having that scene coming to a disturbing close with a kettle’s eerie whistle as it comes to the boil.

articles.title: Kennedy’s Future: Will Democrats Try to Impeach Him, or Actually Work With Him?
articles.summary: Most Democrats abhor the health secretary’s stance on vaccines, but some see an opportunity to win voters from his MAHA movement by joining with him on food and environmental issues.
body: Sheryl Gay Stolberg covers Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and his MAHA movement.

Three days after last week’s “blue wave” election, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. posted a warning on X to anyone suspecting his Make America Healthy Again movement had been weakened. “It’s time to unleash the Kraken,” he wrote.

The phrase, a reference to the 1981 move “Clash of the Titans” that gained currency in 2020 among far-right internet personalities who claimed Democrats stole the election, suggests Mr. Kennedy will fight for his agenda and has no intention of leaving his job despite the defeat of several MAHA-backed candidates.
The question now is whether Democrats will use their new majorities in Congress to try to push him out.

articles.title: US public workers are fighting to protect their jobs from AI – and some are winning
articles.summary: As governments adopt AI, workers are gaining ground in how it’s used and securing safeguards against its harms. In the shadow of Silicon Valley, workers for the city of Oakland, California, worry the region will deploy AI systems that could increase surveillance and inaccurately evaluate their…
body: “We just want the city administration to really be intentional about how it’s engaging with AI products,” said Julian Ware, an Oakland spatial data administrator and member of International Federation of Professional and Technical Engineers Local 21. “Sometimes with a fancy new toy, it actually costs more, it’s more difficult to implement and the results are not as good.”

The nearly unanimous vote had an impact. The city government of Oakland and the union reached a tentative, three-year agreement that includes AI-related protections, such as requiring the city to retrain or reassign workers displaced by AI rather than firing them. As a result, the 5 November strike has been put on hold.

The Bay Area union is one of many public-sector labor groups nationwide seeking explicit protections against AI and automation, which union representatives say could worsen working conditions and threaten jobs. Following decades of automation efforts by companies and growing concern about AI since ChatGPT’s debut in 2022, ongoing labor disputes reveal hardening battle lines between public-sector bosses and their increasingly vocal workers.

articles.title: When the after dinner mints come out, we’re back in our childhood again | Melanie Tait
articles.summary: Australians of a certain age will all remember their parents ending dinner parties with the thin, chocolate-covered squares. It’s an almost world-class error to volunteer the dessert for a meal with friends, when your only talent for dessert is the eating of it and you have $20 in your bank account…
body: Still, that was the unenviable position I found myself in recently. Blaming Donald Trump and his ridiculous wars for my lack of disposable income, I made my way to the supermarket, hoping there would be grapes and berries aplenty to make a fruit plate.

Plastic gleaming in the bright supermarket lighting, forest green boxes somehow whispering: “I’m what you need for your dinner party … I’m what everyone needs for every dinner party … I bring the dinner party … I am the dinner party.”

The box was filled with what Australians have been calling “after-dinner mints” since Red Tulip chocolates launched the After Dinner Mint in 1965, its … ahem … “tribute” to the UK’s Rowntree After Eights which had been a confectionery revolution when it hit the shelves in 1962 (after the Michelangelo of chocolatiers, Yorkshireman Brian Sollitt, discovered how to keep the mint fondant from leaking out of the chocolate casing).

If you grew up between 1965 and 2000, and your parents had other parents over for dinner, you knew the night was ending when the after-dinner mints were served on a tray beside a few cups of instant coffee, a small jug of milk and a bowl of sugar cubes.

articles.title: Hospitals Brace for Medicaid Work Rules and Deep Funding Cuts
articles.summary: Eskenazi Hospital in Indianapolis is dispatching teams into the city’s low-income neighborhoods to help educate patients on keeping their Medicaid coverage.
body: Hospitals across the country are mobilizing an expansive outreach effort in an attempt to ensure that roughly 19 million patients do not lose their insurance coverage under new Medicaid work rules that begin in January.

Saying the requirements are generating widespread anxiety and confusion, health care executives are using a variety of methods to help guide the Americans who will be affected. They are deploying staff and volunteers to contact patients with text messages, phone calls and offers of help.

The rules dictate that able-bodied adults without young children either work, volunteer or attend school or job training for at least 80 hours a month. Republicans included the rules last year as part of President Trump’s package of tax cuts and reductions in safety net spending, including nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts.
Hospitals and other health centers are detailing what evidence people in many cases must provide — pay stubs or other proof of work or school attendance — to maintain coverage.

articles.title: Help! A Broken Toilet Grounded My Plane, and the Airline Won’t Cover a Hotel.
articles.summary: Turkish Airlines tried to wiggle out of paying for a passenger’s $512 overnight stay after a stomach-churning malfunction forced it to cancel a flight in Denver.
body: How an airline describes the cause of a cancellation can directly affect whether it will cover passengers’ lodging, transportation and meals. For mechanical issues, the answer is often yes; for weather or air-traffic issues, it’s almost always no.

U.S. regulations define those categories, but they do not require airlines to pay for stranded passengers’ expenses. Nevertheless, all the major U.S. carriers except Frontier explicitly promise hotel stays in their customer service plans if the reason for the disruption is under their control. The Turkish Airlines policy for U.S. flights is a bit looser — but the airline usually offers lodging for controllable disruptions.

For the last couple of years, I’ve kept a file of emails from travelers who suspected, as you do, that a carrier had weaseled its way out of covering passengers’ expenses by misrepresenting what happened.

articles.title: What to Know About New Prostate Cancer Screening Recommendations
articles.summary: Universal screening for the disease has long been a subject of controversy.
body: The American Cancer Society on Thursday issued new guidelines recommending that all men ages 50 to 69 undergo prostate cancer screening using a blood test every two years.
Black men and those with a strong family history of prostate cancer should start annual screening at 45, the guidelines said.

Universal screening for prostate cancer, which accounts for about 2.5 percent of all deaths among U.S. men, has long been a subject of controversy. The evidence of the benefits of regular testing of blood levels of prostate specific antigen, or P.S.A., is somewhat limited. And there are well-documented harms associated with diagnosing and treating all prostate cancers, which are typically slow growing and may not ever cause issues in men who have them.
The new guidelines diverge from earlier recommendations that patients and physicians decide together about screening, based on careful consideration of the risks and benefits and patients’ values.

articles.summary: To celebrate the Cruise collection’s launch and upcoming trunk show on the luxury e-tailer, the occasion called for a glitzy bash at the newish Nolita haunt.
body: “That couch over there is quite long, and a long couch always leads to long conversations,” Alex Consani whispered, gesturing to the banquette lining Oriana’s amber walls. The supermodel was correct, as guests gathered there en masse to chat all night long. The topic on everyone’s lips? GucciCore, which debuted in Times Square earlier this year, has landed on Moda Operandi.

Gucci’s creative director Demna has a fondness for mystery and enigma—and guests exuded that elusive after-dark glamour as they began to populate the room. Yai did indeed show up, cloaked in a voluminous shearling Gucci coat. Nicky Hilton slinked past her, donning a sharply cut bomber jacket from the new drop. Lauren Santo Domingo, the mastermind behind Moda, posed with poise in the collection’s cinched blazer. And the likes of Tina Leung and Sabine Getty, who had walked the runway in Milan several weeks ago for Demna’s Spring 2027 outing, also stopped by.

articles.title: Why I’m Still Turning to Oils for Thinning Hair
articles.summary: Hair oils do more than just hydrate and nourish strands; they can also help hair look fuller. Here, experts break down the five best hair oils for thinning hair.
body: Much like the internal debate over whether to get curtain bangs or dramatically chop off all your hair into a bob, there comes a point in everyone’s life when they start considering using an oil for thinning hair. Personally, I started my own hair oil journey after noticing sparse patches along my hairline. Many have praised these natural oils for their ability to not only treat breakage and damage but also to help hair grow back. So, I figured, why not try these so-called hair miracle products?

While I personally noticed an improvement in my hair density, experts say to temper your expectations. “It is important to recognize that not all oils have been clinically proven to stimulate new hair growth,” says Marisa Garshick, MD, board-certified dermatologist at MDCS Dermatology. “Rosemary oil and pumpkin seed oil have some preliminary research supporting their potential benefits, while others, such as castor, argan, and jojoba oils, are more beneficial for moisturizing the scalp, strengthening the hair shaft, and reducing breakage.”

articles.title: Ateez’s Yeosang Shares His Anti-Acne Routine
articles.summary: “Doing this video with Vogue made me realize I use quite a lot of products compared to others,” the singer jokes in his Beauty Secrets video.
body: Acne: It happens to the best of us. And that includes, believe it or not, K-pop megastars. When Yeosang, a member of the Korean boy band Ateez, invited Vogue into his bathroom to spill his Beauty Secrets, breakouts were a major topic.

“It used to be a massive source of stress for me,” the singer confesses. “I would constantly agonize over how I could get rid of all of these breakouts on my face.” That’s where a regimented skin-care routine came in. First, he researched ingredients and products—and luckily for him, he had access to one of the world’s best beauty markets.

His routine includes some products you may recognize (“This [product] helps dissolve dead skin cells and tighten pores,” he says about Stridex pads), along with some new discoveries. By the end of the video, though, you’ll probably have discovered a new product or two, plus a trick for using it.

articles.title: Warby Parker Toasted Its New Intelligent Eyewear Pop-Up with a Book-Filled Celebration
articles.summary: The NoHo space serves as an introduction to the new AI-powered Intelligent Eyewear glasses, proudly unveiled by Warby Parker’s co-founders and co-CEOs Neil Blumenthal and Dave Gilboa this week.
body: At first glance, classic literature and artificial intelligence might seem like two topics on opposite ends of the spectrum. On Tuesday evening, however, Warby Parker proved they overlap—and share a sense of wonder and discovery. Those tenets are also core to the brand’s new Literatureland pop-up, now open to the public at 666 Broadway in Manhattan’s NoHo neighborhood.

“We’ve always thought, ‘Is there an evolution of glasses that can help you experience the world even more deeply?’” Blumenthal told Vogue at the celebration. “We’ve just been waiting for technology to emerge—on the hardware side, with the miniaturization of things like batteries and computer chips, and on the software side, with something that provides real utility and can help you navigate the world and answer questions. We’re at that nexus where you can design a beautiful pair of glasses and leverage technology to see beyond what you’d ordinarily be able to see.”

articles.title: Nintendo's Black Friday Deals Are Actually Pretty Good
articles.summary: Black Friday is nearly upon us. From now through Cyber Monday, retailers and companies alike are offering deals and discounts on their wares. While I always keep an eye out for Nintendo deals offered by stores like Amazon and Best Buy, it seems the company is offering its own discounts this year…
body: On Thursday, Nintendo announced its Black Friday discounts. We've already seen Switch 2 sales ahead of the Black Friday season, but now, Nintendo has confirmed an official discount for the console. Starting Nov. 22 through Dec. 5, you can pick up Nintendo's Switch 2 Mario Kart bundle for $499.99, down $50 from $549.99. That includes the console, a download of Mario Kart World, and a 90-day Nintendo Switch Online Individual Membership.

Nintendo rarely offers official discounts on some of its biggest titles, especially in this current era. Games like Donkey Kong Bananza retail for upwards of $69.99, so you're saving as much as $30 on these games during this week-long promotion. In addition, Nintendo announced a sale on its digital store that runs from Nov. 19 through Dec. 2, though it didn't say which titles would be on sale. Just keep an eye on all these dates: The Switch 2 console promotion runs longer than the physical and digital games discounts, while the digital sale runs longer than the physical sale.
